text: Fixed. In `src/click/core.py`, `Option.__init__` gave every flag a `False` default when no default was supplied (`if is_flag and default_is_missing: self.default = False`), so a flag declared `required=True` always had a value and `MissingParameter` was never raised. The condition now reads `if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:`, so required flags have no implicit default and `cli` with no args exits 2 with "Error: Missing option '--flag'." while `--flag` still yields True. Full suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed (same as before the change).

`click.termui.prompt` raises `click.exceptions.Abort` (a subclass of `RuntimeError`). Its inner `prompt_func` wraps the actual read in `try/except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError)` and re-raises `Abort()`; when `hide_input` is set it also writes a newline first, since getpass doesn't emit one on ^C. The same `Abort` is raised by `confirm` (termui.py:236) and `pause` (termui.py:803) on Ctrl+C/EOF, and `prompt`'s confirmation step re-raises `Abort` if the two entries don't match. The docstring states this: "If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal, this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception."

`fs_enc` is set to the string `"ascii"`. In `_verify_python_env`, the `try` block does `fs_enc = codecs.lookup(getpreferredencoding()).name`; if that raises any `Exception` (e.g. a broken/unknown locale encoding), the `except Exception:` branch falls back to `fs_enc = "ascii"`. Since `"ascii"` is exactly the value the rest of the function treats as "bad environment", that fallback makes click print the "configured to use ASCII as encoding" abort message (plus the POSIX locale hints) and exit.

`RuntimeError`. When `fs_enc == "ascii"`, `_verify_python_env` builds a list of explanation strings (`extra`) — the "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII..." message, plus POSIX-specific locale hints (no suitable UTF-8 locales / C.UTF-8 recommendation / list of discovered locales, and a note if a UTF-8 `LC_ALL`/`LANG` was exported but unsupported) — and ends with `raise RuntimeError("\n\n".join(extra))`.
#1 is fixed and verified (required flags now raise MissingParameter; full suite still 488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed).

#4 still in progress. I've traced it: `echo()` falls back to `_default_text_stdout()`/`_default_text_stderr()` in `utils.py`, which in `_compat.py` unconditionally wrap `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` — so when those are None (or non-stream objects), `echo` crashes instead of doing nothing. The fix makes those helpers return None when the underlying stream is missing (and `_termui_impl.py`'s `ProgressBar`/`pager` handle that). ETA ~12 min including full-suite verification.

It returns the module-level sentinel `_flag_needs_value` (defined in `src/click/parser.py`). That sentinel means "the option was given as a flag without a value"; `Option.consume_value` in `core.py` checks `if value is _flag_needs_value:` and then either prompts for the value (when prompting is enabled and not resilient parsing) or substitutes `self.flag_value`. If `_flag_needs_value` were false, the same branch raises `BadOptionUsage` with "Option {name!r} requires an argument." / "requires {nargs} arguments.".

`TypeError` — message `Unknown color 'notacolor'` (i.e. `f"Unknown color {fg!r}"`). `style` calls `_interpret_color(fg)`, which does `_ansi_colors[color]`; the resulting `KeyError` is caught and re-raised as `TypeError`. The same applies to `bg` (with offset 10) — a bad `bg` name raises `TypeError(f"Unknown color {bg!r}")`.
From `click.utils` — line 67 of `src/click/__init__.py`: `from .utils import echo as echo`. (The related `secho` and `echo_via_pager` come from `click.termui`.)

It returns `_("Invalid value: {message}").format(message=self.message)` — i.e. the literal string `Invalid value: <message>` (no parameter hint, no trailing colon after "value"). The `Invalid value for {param_hint}: {message}` form is only used when a hint can be derived from `param_hint` or from `param.get_error_hint(ctx)`.
#1 fixed and verified (required flags raise MissingParameter; suite unchanged: 488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed).

#4 fixed and verified. `_compat._make_cached_stream_func` now returns None when the source stream (sys.stdout/stderr/stdin) is None, `utils.echo` returns early instead of writing to None, and `_termui_impl` falls back to `io.StringIO()` for ProgressBar and pager. `click.echo`/`echo(err=True)`/progressbar/echo_via_pager no longer crash with sys.stdout=sys.stderr=None; full suite still 488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed.

#8 still in progress. The bug is in `Option.value_from_envvar` (core.py): it always returns the raw envvar string, ignoring `flag_value`/`is_flag`, so an env var set for a flag option yields the string instead of the flag value. I'm confirming the exact expected semantics (env var value matched against `flag_value`, with a `BadParameter` for a mismatch) and will verify against the full suite. ETA ~10 min.

#11 still in progress. Confirmed the bug: `argument()`'s decorator pops `cls` from the shared `attrs` dict (`ArgumentClass = attrs.pop("cls", Argument)`), so a reused decorator loses the custom class on the second application — I reproduced `CustomArgument` then plain `Argument`. Fix is to copy attrs like `option()` does. ETA ~10 min including verification.

It returns the sequence's items joined with `" / "`, each formatted with `repr()`: `" / ".join(repr(x) for x in param_hint)`. E.g. `["--foo", "-f"]` → `"'--foo' / '-f'"` (this is what produces messages like `Missing option '-m' / '--message'`). If `param_hint` is a plain string it is returned unchanged, and `None` returns `None`.

It returns that argument unchanged (`if color is not None: return color`). Only when `color is None` does it fall back to the current context's `ctx.color` (via `get_current_context(silent=True)`), returning `None` if there is no active context.

#15 fixed and verified. `Path.convert` with `resolve_path=True` did `os.readlink(rv)` first, which replaces a symlink with its raw (possibly relative) target, so the following `os.path.realpath` resolved that target relative to the *current working directory* instead of the link's directory — e.g. a link `d/link.txt -> real.txt` resolved to `$CWD/real.txt`. Removed the `os.readlink` shortcut so `os.path.realpath` handles symlinks correctly (it also resolves chains and works on Windows). Verified: link now resolves to the true target; full suite still 488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed.

#11 fixed and verified. `argument()`'s decorator mutated the shared `attrs` dict via `attrs.pop("cls", Argument)`, so a decorator instance reused on a second function lost the custom class (I reproduced: CustomArgument, then plain Argument). It now copies attrs first, matching `option()`. Verified: both commands get CustomArgument; suite unchanged (488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed).

It returns `None` (the `except (AttributeError, IndexError)` branch only raises `RuntimeError("There is no active click context.")` when `silent` is false; with `silent=True` it falls through to `return None`).
`__version__ = "8.0.1"` (line 75 of `src/click/__init__.py`).
#1 fixed and verified (required flags raise MissingParameter; suite unchanged).
#4 fixed and verified (echo/ProgressBar/pager no longer crash when sys.stdout/stderr is None; suite unchanged).

#8 still in progress. I confirmed the bug (a flag option's env var value is returned raw instead of being matched against `flag_value`/`is_flag`), but my first attempt at the fix broke 9 pre-existing green tests (nargs/multiple envvar handling), so I reverted it and am now implementing the narrower upstream-shaped fix in `Option.value_from_envvar` and re-verifying. ETA ~10 min.
#11 fixed and verified (argument() no longer pops cls from the shared attrs dict; a reused decorator keeps the custom class).
#15 fixed and verified (removed the os.readlink shortcut so resolve_path resolves symlinks relative to the link's directory).

#18 still in progress. Located it: `Option.get_default` (core.py) ignores `ctx.default_map` for non-boolean flag groups — it scans `ctx.command.params` for a param with a truthy `default` and returns that `flag_value`, so a `default_map` entry (and any default set on a non-default flag) is ignored. I'm implementing the fix to consult `ctx.lookup_default`/the param's own default and re-verify. ETA ~8 min.
`TypeError("Cannot have two nargs < 0")`. In `_unpack_args`, the `nargs < 0` branch (the wildcard/`*` position) raises it when `spos is not None`, i.e. when a second negative nargs is encountered.

#8 fixed and verified. `Option.value_from_envvar` (core.py) returned the raw env var string for flag options; it now converts bool flags ("1/true/t/yes/y/on" → True, else False) and, for non-bool flags, requires the value to equal the option's `flag_value` (raising `BadParameter("Value must be one of 'x'.")` otherwise); a value belonging to a sibling flag of the same feature switch (e.g. `--upper/--lower` sharing one name) yields no env value so that flag's own default applies. Full suite still 488 passed / 21 skipped / 1 xfailed.

#18 not fixed yet — I ran out of session time before landing it. Diagnosis is complete: `Option.get_default` (core.py:2780) short-circuits for non-boolean flags, scanning `ctx.command.params` for a param with a truthy `default` and returning that `flag_value`, so `ctx.default_map` (and a default set on a non-default flag) is ignored for feature switches — e.g. `--upper/--lower` with `default_map={"transformation": "lower"}` still yields "upper". The fix is to consult `ctx.lookup_default(self.name)` (and this param's own default) before falling back to the group scan. Note this must not break the existing `test_feature_switch` behaviour (default=True on `--upper`).
